correctness.rationale: For x>=y>=0 the first folded component is x-h(y). Subtracting the second component yields either x-y+h(x)-h(y) or (x-h(x))+(y-h(y)), both nonnegative. Applying the ordered formula twice gives x-h(y)-h(|y-h(x)|). The subtracted sum is at least a(y+|y-h(x)|)>=a h(x)>=a²x. One-step nonincrease handles odd horizons. For h(t)=at, the boundary orbit maps (x,0) to (x,ax) and then ((1-a²)x,0), including a=1 with the zero-exponent convention. Continuity gives the positive-start supremum. For softplus, h(epsilon t)/epsilon tends to t/2 uniformly on bounded t; the rescaled starts (1,epsilon) and their fixed finite iterates stay bounded by the one-step estimate and converge to those of the linear corner orbit. At nonzero x, h(x)>x/2 makes the two-step estimate strictly smaller; at n=1 and positive inputs h(y)>0. In physical coordinates inverse logit has derivative at most 1/4; Satur's actual recurrence agrees exactly at alpha=2. The statement is toward the origin, not pairwise contraction.
